title: Zariski local affine etale atlases of an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. There is a set-indexed Zariski covering $X=\bigcup_iX_i$ by open subspaces such that each $X_i$ admits a representable surjective etale morphism $h_{U_i}\to X_i$ with $U_i$ an affine scheme. Moreover each $X_i\to S$ factors through an affine open subscheme of $S$. Here an open subspace is a subfunctor whose inclusion is representable and becomes an open immersion on every scheme base change [def-weil-open-immersion], and a Zariski covering means that their underlying open subsets cover the field-valued point classes of $X$. A field-valued point class means a map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ with $K$ a field, with two such maps identified when they agree over a common field extension; the underlying set of an open subspace is the set of classes that factor through it.

source.place: Tag 03FY (lemma-union-of-quasi-compact), including the final affine-base clause.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $p:h_V\to X$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The final clause of [lem-a1-space-atlas-open-refinement-pullback], applied to this prescribed atlas, supplies affine opens $U_i\subseteq V$ covering $V$ and affine opens $W_i\subseteq S$ with structural factorizations $U_i\to W_i\to S$. For a scheme test $h_T\to X$, the same node represents the chart pullback by $P_i=(T\times_XV)\times_VU_i$ and makes $P_i\to T\times_XV$ an open immersion. The second projection is etale by the scheme-test definition of $p$. Clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] therefore make $P_i\to T$ etale. Thus each $f_i:h_{U_i}\to X$ is representable etale.

source.place: Tag 03FX (lemma-cover-by-union-affines), proof: choosing the affine open pieces of a fixed atlas over affine base opens and verifying etaleness by scheme-test pullback, before forming the coproduct.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-etale-scheme-map-open-image] to each $f_i$. This gives an open subspace $X_i\subseteq X$ and a representable surjective etale factor $a_i:h_{U_i}\to X_i$, with $|X_i|=\operatorname{im}(|U_i|\to|X|)$. For the same prescribed atlas $p$ and the same family $(U_i)$, [lem-a1-space-atlas-open-refinement-pullback] also states that the composite $w:h_{\coprod_iU_i}\to X$ has $|w|$ surjective. Every point of $\coprod_iU_i$ lies in one open component $\iota_i(U_i)$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and $w$ restricted to that component is $f_i$; so the images of the $|U_i|$, that is the $|X_i|$, cover $|X|$. Thus the $X_i$ give the required Zariski covering with affine atlases.

source.place: Tags 06NF (lemma-etale-image-open) and 03FY (lemma-union-of-quasi-compact), construction of the open images and covering assertion.

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-a1-surjective-chart-base-open-factorization] with $Y=X_i$, $q=a_i$, $U=U_i$ and $W=W_i$. Its hypotheses hold because $a_i$ is representable surjective and the structural map of $U_i$ already factors through $W_i$. It supplies $X_i\to h_{W_i}$ over $S$, proving the affine-base clause. The construction includes the empty-atlas case by the empty family.

source.place: Tag 03FY (lemma-union-of-quasi-compact), final proof sentence: descent of the factorization through an affine base open; the same scheme-test argument applies to any open W and representable surjection.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03FY (lemma-union-of-quasi-compact), with the affine-piece construction from Tag 03FX and open-image input Tag 06NF; final factorization written on scheme tests.

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_atlas_open_cover {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) : ∃ (I : Type u) (Xi : I → AlgebraicSpace S) (j : ∀ i : I, Xi i ⟶ X) (U : I → Over S) (a : ∀ i : I, yoneda.obj (U i) ⟶ (Xi i).obj.obj), IsJointlySurjective (fun i : I ↦ (j i).hom.hom) ∧ ∀ i : I, IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) (j i).hom.hom ∧ IsAffine (U i).left ∧ IsEtale (a i) ∧ IsSurjective (a i) ∧ ∃ W : S.Opens, IsAffine W.toScheme ∧ Nonempty ((Xi i).obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk W.ι))
